entities.name: Thomas Webster
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Thomas Webster (1773–1844) was a Scottish geologist, architect, and scientific illustrator who played a formative role in early British stratigraphy, especially of the Isle of Wight and the London Basin. Trained in architectural drawing, he brought precise draftsmanship to geological sections and museum display, serving as curator and lecturer in London scientific institutions including the Geological Society milieu.

Webster’s mapping of Tertiary strata and coastal structures helped British geology move from mineral collecting toward ordered rock succession—work that complemented contemporaries such as William Smith’s broader stratigraphic project. His dual identity as architect-draughtsman and geologist made him unusually effective at visualising underground structure for public and specialist audiences.

He stands among the practical founders of English regional geology in the generation that professionalised earth science before Darwinian fame reshaped natural history.
